Usually I wake up with brain fog that doesn't actually start subsiding for about 30-60 mins after I wake up. I woke up this morning with no brain fog, though. I had a couple of slices of Marmite on toast last night at about 11pm before going to bed. I have not had Marmite for several years before last night, however.

The perceived effects of the Marmite from this morning led me to Google whether Marmite has an effect on brain function. Imagine my surprise when I found this article, published about three weeks ago, documenting a scientific study on exactly that. Subjects ate a teaspoon of Marmite every day for a month, and the results were that they showed a substantial reduction of around 30 per cent in their brain’s response to visual stimuli.

Apparently, this is due to Marmite having a lot of vitamin B12. This vitamin increases levels of a neurotransmitter in the brain called GABA, which has links to impulsivity and inhibition. Increases in GABA in the brain supposedly decrease your compulsion to react to things around you. Another paper shows that people with ADHD have a deficit in GABA.

This is far from scientifically proven, as I said, but it is nonetheless interesting. Who here likes Marmite? Have you noticed any changes in your brain after eating it?
